This is an evidence gap, not evidence that AI cannot write adequate memos.

statement.document_title: In the Iran war, it looks like AI helped with operations, not strategy

from_speaker: AI is fine for writing memos
our_interpretation: Assess only the memo-writing proposition identified in this claim, not the separate recommendation against relying on AI to plan wars.
The plain reading is that conversational generative AI can produce usable routine memo drafts with ordinary human review.
Adequacy means coherent, useful writing that follows the brief and handles supplied facts accurately; it does not imply flawless autonomous research.
For this ongoing claim, the target is March 2026, the latest complete month before publication.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations of target-period systems show that routine memo drafts generally meet ordinary professional requirements for accuracy, coherence and usefulness with normal review.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations show that target-period systems routinely fail those requirements even when given adequate instructions and source facts.

evidence.publisher: MIT; Shakked Noy and Whitney Zhang
evidence.explanation: The experiment found benefits on short professional writing assignments assessed by blinded professionals. It provides relevant historical support for writing assistance, but neither measures March 2026 systems nor reports a distinct memo-writing adequacy result.
The release reports stronger document capabilities and aggregate professional-work performance. Those broader results do not isolate routine memos or establish their factual accuracy and usability.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated evaluation of March 2026 systems on realistic routine memos, with professional assessments of accuracy, coherence, usefulness and the editing required.
